structural.why: UX-I-32 (Major, duplicate-feature) — HeadersScreen.tsx:268-280 renders its own primary AND registers with the central savebar (:119), so two identical-in-effect, differently-labelled Saves are live at once. One Save, in one place: the savebar. NOTE the script reports NOT-DRAWN rather than failing where the board never drew this button — FIG-M-21 says 2209:11816 draws a header 'Save changes' instead, and that node is deleted by the header pass. CONFLICT RESOLVED IN THIS PASS (UX-I-32 vs COVER-1-11): COVER-1-11 asks the four save-failure boards to be redrawn as the full screen with the error at the foot ‘beside Save headers’ / ‘beside Save locales’ — i.e. WITH the very button UX-I-32 removes. Both cannot land as written. Decision: UX-I-32 wins the button, COVER-1-11 keeps its substance. COVER-1-11's real claim is that a save failure is never an early return and the whole form stays on screen; only the anchor for the error line moves, from the in-body Save to the savebar's single Save. COVER-1-11 is UNAPPLIED today (register: PENDING; its redraw is manual-draw class), so nothing is being undone — its instruction is amended in one line, recorded as an advisory row in gap-a-triage.json so its future owner sees it.
